data.translation:
United Airlines Bans Ticket Bookings by AI Assistants over Cybersecurity Risks

United Airlines announced that it would restrict access to its systems for AI tools seeking to book flights and manage ticket transactions on behalf of users. The company cited cybersecurity risks and the potential for violations of federal aviation regulations as the reasons for its decision.

Recently, companies in the aviation and finance sectors have been finding it increasingly difficult to distinguish between real customers and autonomous AI systems acting on their behalf. In a statement, United Airlines emphasized that sharing account login credentials with third-party personal AI assistants could put sensitive data at risk. The company noted that automated actions taken by these tools could lead to unwanted purchases, account changes, or the unauthorized use of MileagePlus miles from its passenger loyalty program.

Another key factor behind the decision was federal aviation regulations. Under current rules, pre-flight check-in must be performed by a human, and passengers must personally confirm that their baggage contains no prohibited items.

United Airlines, which has updated its flight booking, ticketing, and distribution policies, said it had taken the necessary steps to ban unauthorized AI assistants on both its own digital platforms and those of travel agencies and ticket aggregators. Bank of America recently took a similar measure, asking customers not to share their passwords with AI assistants.

United Airlines, Siber Güvenlik Riskleri Gerekçesiyle Yapay Zeka Asistanlarıyla Bilet Rezervasyonunu Yasakladı

United Airlines, kullanıcılar adına uçuş rezervasyonu yapmak ve bilet işlemlerini yönetmek isteyen yapay zeka araçlarının sistemlerine erişimini kısıtlayacağını duyurdu. Şirket, bu karara gerekçe olarak siber güvenlik risklerini ve federal havacılık kurallarının ihlal edilme potansiyelini gösterdi.

Son dönemde havacılık ve finans sektöründeki şirketler, gerçek müşteriler ile onların adına işlem yapan otonom yapay zeka sistemlerini ayırt etmekte giderek daha fazla zorlanıyor. United Airlines tarafından yapılan açıklamada, hesap giriş bilgilerinin üçüncü taraf kişisel yapay zeka asistanlarıyla paylaşılmasının hassas verileri tehlikeye atabileceği vurgulandı. Şirket, bu araçlar tarafından otomatik olarak atılacak adımların istenmeyen satın alımlara, hesap değişikliklerine veya yolcu sadakat programı MileagePlus millerinin kontrolsüz kullanımına yol açabileceğini belirtti.

Kararın arkasında yatan bir diğer önemli etken ise federal havacılık kuralları oldu. Mevcut düzenlemelere göre, uçuş öncesi check-in işlemlerinin bir insan tarafından yapılması ve bagajlarda yasaklı madde bulunmadığının yolcu tarafından bizzat onaylanması gerekiyor.

Uçuş rezervasyonu, biletleme ve dağıtım politikalarını güncelleyen United Airlines, hem şirketin kendi dijital platformlarında hem de seyahat acenteleri ile biletleyici platformlar (aggregator) üzerinde yetkisiz yapay zeka asistanlarının kullanımını yasaklamak için gerekli adımları attığını bildirdi. Benzer bir önlem yakın zamanda Bank of America tarafından da alınmış ve müşterilerden parolalarını yapay zeka asistanlarıyla paylaşmamaları talep edilmişti.

result.text:
🤖 AI-driven payments raise fraud fears across the banking sector
Meta's AI agents, including Muse and Instinct, have recently gained the ability to make purchases using consumers' credit cards. While adoption is still limited, payments executives expect agent-driven transactions to grow significantly, the Wall Street Journal reports.
Banks, payment networks, and merchants are far from agreeing on how to handle this new reality:
🔴 Stripe bets on agentic commerce, positioning its Link digital wallet, with more than 300 million users, as a key infrastructure layer for AI-driven purchases
🔴 JPMorgan - the largest US credit-card issuer by purchase volume—has been slow to adopt some of the emerging payment solutions, restricting AI agents from shopping with customers' cards
🔴 Other major banks are moving ahead cautiously, as cards issued by Bank of America, Capital One, and Citigroup are already being used by AI agents when customers authorize them
The shift to AI assistants is raising a whole array of concerns, including higher fraud risks, such as purchases from fake online stores, as well as unclear liability when AI agents make purchases on behalf of customers and higher fees for merchants using virtual cards.
The industry is also experimenting with agentic tokens — digital credentials designed to conceal actual card numbers while carrying information about spending limits and user permissions.
Meanwhile, the divide extends beyond payments: Amazon has blocked Meta's Muse from making purchases, and United Airlines plans to prevent personal AI assistants from accessing its booking systems. Walmart, by contrast, says it will allow authorized AI agents to shop on its platform.

result.text:
US stock market today, Friday 13 November, before the 9:30 am open.

Wholesale inflation. Producer prices rose 0.3% in October, under the 0.4% economists had forecast (BLS). Over 12 months they are up 6.5%, the most since November 2022. Core prices, without food and energy, rose 0.3%, in line with economists, 5.0% over the year. Traders priced in less Fed tightening after the report. Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee told CNBC inflation is "broad-based" and "going the wrong way", and that the Fed is not on track to reach 2%. Bank of America now forecasts Fed hikes in December, January and March. Treasury Secretary Bessent called it an energy supply shock and said core inflation is under control. The 10-year Treasury yield was 5.14%.

Futures. S&P 500 futures +0.4%, Nasdaq 100 futures +0.2% vs Thursday's settle.

Nvidia. $169.89 before the bell at 9:15 am, up 2.2% from Thursday's $166.19 close. Bessent on CNBC: Nvidia is "a fantastic company" and "can move on from founder". He asked whether Nvidia knew its clients, and said Treasury pushed for months to blacklist Megaspeed but Commerce did not add it. Commerce Secretary Lutnick has agreed to testify to the Senate Banking Committee on 10 December (Fox Business). AMD -2.9% pre-market.

Oil and Iran. Brent $96.84, up from Thursday's $95.82 settle. The IEA says oil supply is now beating demand for the first time since the Iran war began: stockpiles rose 52 million barrels in October, and member countries plan to release 71 million more barrels of emergency stocks by February. CENTCOM says US forces shot down two Iranian drones launched toward Bahrain. Axios: Israel's Mossad chief is in Washington as Netanyahu presses to resume the war.

Crypto. Bitcoin fell under $70,000 for the first time since August, to a low near $68,050; Bloomberg tied it to higher bond yields.

Source: BLS · Yahoo Finance · IEA · CENTCOM · CNBC · Bloomberg · Axios · Fox Business.
